chose: 3.1 CONTRACT (the prompt-time BM25 index), with the TypeScript reference first and rust-core mirroring it as 3.4.
(a) CORPUS: repo-wide. It covers every decision (chose + over + because, clipped to 1,200 chars) and every note (clipped to 1,200 chars) in every initiative, plus this record's stall handoffs as today. IDF runs over the whole corpus, retired entries included, so postings stay append-only. Retired entries are dropped only at render: own-record ones through retiredOrdinals(state), other records' through the tier's own supersession marks (stamped id first, memory-lead D12). Another record's until-scoped decisions are excluded outright, because whether their task resolved is not indexed.
(b) TIER: .sofar/.index/lexicon.json with meta-lexicon.json, maintained incrementally through passOverRecord, stamped with the existing INDEX_SCHEMA_VERSION and no bump (no existing shape changes). Per slug it holds a doc table (kind, ordinal, ts, token count, render heads clipped to 300 chars) and postings from term to flat [doc, tf, inOver]. Reducers gain an optional `relevant(event)`. A batch with no relevant event carries the state by reference and does not rewrite the file, so appending command_run never rewrites the tier.
(c) RENDER, at most 2 lines, with LESSON_MIN_TERMS, LESSON_MIN_SCORE, the young-record rule and the runner-up ratio unchanged. A decision whose matched terms occur in its `over` renders `sofar: ruled out before — [<h>] <over>`. Otherwise it renders `sofar: decided before — [<h>] chose <chose>`. A note renders `sofar: noted before — [<h>] <text>`. Every line ends in `(matched: …)`. <h> is D<n> for this record, `<slug> D<n>` for another, and `<slug> note <date>` for a note.
(d) TOLD ONCE per (session, doc) through core/told with the subject `prompt`. A lost set re-tells and never silences, and compact or clear empties it (memory-lead D6).
(e) FALLBACK AND ABLATION: an unreadable tier falls back to today's own-fold path (last 60 decisions). SOFAR_LESSONS=off disables the line, and SOFAR_LESSONS=fold forces the old path: the ablation arm that prices the index apart from r1-fixes 3.3 (r1-fixes D5).
PREDICT: C3 re-violation −30% relative to the fold-only line on Chain L's superseded and why-only probes, and cross-record re-proposals caught where the old line caught 0. Tokens +<1% (≤2 lines, told once). User-prompt p50 within D18's +10%. The rust-core lane measures that after the smokes (3.2/3.4). If it is over budget, the index defaults to `fold`.
over: (1) Keeping the per-prompt tokenizing of the fold and raising the 60-decision cap: the cost is proportional to prose, about 90 ms at this repo's 1,100 docs. (2) Reusing reach.json: 1.6 MB parsed on every prompt. (3) Embeddings: they are barred without a Decision, and they cannot show which words carried a match. (4) Removing retired docs from postings: that breaks the append-only resume. (5) Two docs per decision, split into chose and over: a re-proposal phrased in the subject's words would no longer reach its rejection (the r1-fixes 3.3 finding). (6) Indexing memory entries now: they are already in the digest, and they would widen the scope past the task.
because: r1-fixes 3.3's line reads only this record's last 60 decisions and renders only `over`. It misses the cross-record re-proposals behind cursor-sofar's A2 loss, and every rejection older than 60 decisions. It also cannot surface a note, and notes are where most findings live on this repo (523 notes against 495 decisions). Precomputing terms turns per-prompt tokenizing into a lookup over postings. The `relevant` filter keeps the per-prompt write cost at zero on the common path, where only hooks' mechanical events arrived.
